analysis.title: National Vision Holdings (EYE) 3Q26 recap: Traffic weighs on comp but profitability improves; Store openings to accelerate in FY27
key_insights: EYE rose +2.7% after the 3Q26 print vs -0.4% for the S&P 500. GS attributes the reaction to plans to accelerate FY27 store openings and improving profitability from cost-saving initiatives, despite continued traffic pressure.
3Q26 comp was +2.8%, a miss vs GS consensus of +3.8% and FactSet consensus of +3.4%. Average ticket was +8.9% and customer traffic was -5.6%.

The traffic decline was concentrated in transactions below the average ticket amount, including the entry-level bundle offer. Management said the bottom 25% of transactions by ticket value are only high-single-digit % of total sales and an even lower share of gross profit.
Management frames the weakness as a deferral challenge rather than a market share issue. Repeat-customer purchase cycles extended by about 3 weeks in the quarter vs about 2 weeks in 2Q.
The top 25% of transactions and the managed care customer cohort saw positive traffic and ticket growth.

FY26 SSS guidance was lowered to +2% to +3% from +3% to +5%, reflecting a sequential deceleration in October and continued traffic pressure in lower value transactions. GS now models SSS of +0.5% for 4Q26 and +2.5% for FY26.

Operating margin expanded 320bps in 3Q despite gross margin pressure from a mix shift toward premium products. SG&A leverage was 250bps, from store labor model efficiencies, lower variable incentive compensation and cost optimization.

FY26 adjusted operating income guidance was narrowed to $119mn-$131mn from $119mn-$139mn. At the midpoint this is 110bps of expansion excluding the 53rd week in FY25, within the long-term algorithm of 50-150bps a year.

EYE opened 8 new stores in 3Q, all America's Best, and narrowed FY26 openings to about 30 (excluding military locations). FY26 openings are achieving a materially higher average ticket than prior-year openings.

Management introduced an FY27 opening target of 50-55 stores, about 75% unit growth at the midpoint vs about 30 in FY26. The new flagship store in Alpharetta, GA and other stores in the new format have had positive reception.
GS stays Neutral because of accelerating traffic declines and competitive concerns as EYE leans into higher income, managed care customers. The price target rises to $24 from $23.

GS cut estimates: FY26E adj. EBITDA $224.4mn (from $230.9mn), FY27E $253.2mn (from $253.9mn), FY28E $280.7mn (from $285.3mn), with a new FY29E of $318.7mn. 4Q26E sales were cut 10.4% to $475.0mn and 4Q26E adj. EPS to $0.00 from $0.16.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised its PT to $24 from $23 on estimate changes, with unchanged 8.0x/9.0x/10.0x EV/EBITDA scenario multiples. It stays Neutral because traffic declines are accelerating and competition is a concern, implying 29.2% upside from $18.57.

sector_views.rationale: Traffic is negative as value-seeking customers defer purchases and lower-income and uninsured cohorts are weak, while higher-ticket and managed care customers are growing.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported comp +2.8% vs GS consensus +3.8% and FactSet consensus +3.4% (miss). Ticket +8.9%, traffic -5.6%.
3Q26 operating margin expanded 320bps y/y, with SG&A leverage of 250bps.
FY26 guidance as reported 11/12/26: SSS +2% to +3% (prior +3% to +5%), adj. operating income $119mn-$131mn (prior $119mn-$139mn).

GS estimates (not company guidance): 4Q26E SSS +0.5%, 4Q26E sales $475.0mn, 4Q26E adj. EBITDA $31.4mn, 4Q26E adj. EPS $0.00. FY26E adj. EPS $1.01 (from $1.02), FY27E $1.17 (unchanged), FY28E $1.37 (from $1.42), FY29E $1.67.
GS FY26E revenue is $2,028.2mn (from $2,082.5mn), FY27E $2,126.9mn (from $2,170.5mn), FY28E $2,297.6mn (from $2,319.9mn).
risk_factors: Downside: slower top-line recovery as lower-income and uninsured customers defer demand or exit the market.
Downside: less-than-expected trade down, continued exam capacity headwinds, wage-driven margin pressure, increased competition and persistently elevated costs.
Upside: better-than-expected eye care and eyeglasses demand, faster margin recovery, and a possible multiple re-rating if top-line results beat and the path to margin recovery is clear.

tension_points.bull_case: Operating margin expanded 320bps on 250bps of SG&A leverage, and FY27 store openings are set to accelerate to 50-55 after FY26 openings showed a materially higher average ticket. The stock rose 2.7% on the print.
tension_points.bear_case: Traffic fell 5.6%, comp missed consensus, and FY26 SSS guidance was cut to +2% to +3%. GS cites accelerating traffic declines and competitive risk as EYE pushes into higher income, managed care customers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further sequential deceleration in comps after October's slowdown, or traffic declines spreading to the top 25% of transactions and the managed care cohort.

theme_stances.key_argument: Traffic declines are accelerating as value-seeking customers defer purchases, so GS stays on the sidelines despite better profitability.
theme_stances.evidence: we remain on the sidelines based on accelerating traffic declines
